We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=4{x}^{5} & \,⟹\,v=\int 4{x}^{5}\,dx=\frac{2{x}^{6}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}4{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{2{x}^{6}}{3}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}(\frac{2{x}^{6}}{3})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\frac{2({e}^{3})^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})}{3}-\frac{2(1)^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)}{3}]-\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{18}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})}{3}-\frac{{x}^{6}}{9}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}} \\  & =2{e}^{18}-(\frac{{e}^{18}}{9}-\frac{1}{9}) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(18{e}^{18}-{e}^{18}+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(17{e}^{18}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
